cases.question: If two Java objects are equal according to equals, what must hashCode return? Must unequal objects have different hash codes?
cases.expected_fact: Equal objects must have the same hash code; unequal objects need not have distinct hash codes.
cases.answer:
If two objects are equal according to the equals method, calling the hashCode method on each of the two objects must produce the same integer result. [javaNotesForProfessionals, PDF p. 253]

It is not required that if two objects are unequal according to the equals method, calling the hashCode method on each of the two objects must produce distinct integer results. [javaNotesForProfessionals, PDF p. 253]

cases.question: Do String.toUpperCase and String.toLowerCase modify the original Java String, or return a new String instance?
cases.expected_fact: The original String is not modified because strings are immutable; converted strings are returned as new String instances.
cases.answer:
String.toUpperCase and String.toLowerCase return the converted strings as new String instances. [javaNotesForProfessionals, PDF p. 77]

The original String objects are not modified because String is immutable in Java. [javaNotesForProfessionals, PDF p. 77]

cases.question: Does a file channel tryLock call return immediately, and what indicates that no file lock was acquired?
cases.expected_fact: FileChannel.tryLock returns immediately; null indicates failure to acquire a lock in the example.
cases.answer:
The tryLock call always returns immediately. [javaNotesForProfessionals, PDF p. 484]

A null return value indicates that no file lock was acquired. [javaNotesForProfessionals, PDF p. 484]

cases.question: Why does the custom serialization example declare its Thread field transient, and does deserialization run the constructor again?
cases.expected_fact: Thread is not serializable, so its field is declared transient; readObject restoration does not rerun the constructor in this example.
cases.answer:
The Thread field is declared as transient because it is one of the certain system-level classes that are not Serializable. [javaNotesForProfessionals, PDF p. 404]

Deserialization does not run the constructor again because there is no creation of a new object when restoring the persisted object. [javaNotesForProfessionals, PDF p. 404]
